description:
Goal: reduce pull-request CI latency while retaining the full all-features coverage ratchet and its deterministic signal.

Baseline signal (2026-09-11/12): twelve completed successful CI runs spent a mean 1,654s (27m34s; range 21m16s–33m43s) in cargo llvm-cov, 96.6% of the test job. In run 34703940486, coverage compilation took 52s; fz lib tests took 1,117.42s, fixture_matrix took 656.07s, and fz2 CLI tests took 136.25s.

Current delivery evidence (2026-09-16/17): CI is configured with RUST_TEST_THREADS=4, but that setting is not certified. Coverage runs 35117425156, 35164896337, and 35165073285 failed because json_roundtrip did not signal execution readiness within 20 seconds; the latter also failed execution_guard_covers_the_program_not_the_compile. Nearby main runs passed. The guard is therefore reporting an intermittent readiness or contention defect, not proof that four workers are stable.

The former 3s contention tripwire is now the 20s nontermination guard (fz-kdt.175), and the concurrent AOT runtime-archive mtime race was closed by deterministic archive selection (fz-0lm). fz-zwj remains the direct prerequisite: readiness probes must support multi-digit file descriptors before any worker-count conclusion is trustworthy.

Strategy: preserve the existing cargo llvm-cov command and coverage threshold. After fz-zwj, measure RUST_TEST_THREADS=1, then 2, then 4 with at least five clean GitHub Actions runs for each candidate. Compare successful-run wall time and the exact coverage JSON line percentage; treat readiness timeout, archive/link, temp-file, global-state, output-determinism, and descriptor failures as disqualifying evidence. Choose the fastest stable bounded value, document the rationale beside the workflow setting, update CI timing telemetry/reporting so regressions are visible, and delete the obsolete premise that serial execution is the safe default. Do not move coverage off PRs or weaken the threshold as a shortcut.

Acceptance: the chosen setting passes strict full CI repeatedly; coverage result is unchanged or improves; no readiness or historical parallel-flake class recurs; measured median coverage time is materially below the serial baseline; CI workflow comments/docs state the measured worker count and its timeout/archive/descriptor invariants.
title: CI: restore bounded coverage-test parallelism after resolved contention defects
